checks.titleEn: CTS tracker is enabled
checks.condition: Ensure that Cloud Trace Service (CTS) tracker is enabled to record all API calls and operations performed in the Huawei Cloud account.
checks.remediation: Enable the CTS system tracker to record all API calls and operations in the Huawei Cloud account.

checks.titleEn: ECS instances should use SSH key pairs for authentication
checks.condition: Ensure that Elastic Cloud Server (ECS) instances use SSH key pairs instead of password-based authentication for secure access.
checks.remediation: Bind SSH key pairs to all ECS instances and disable password-based authentication.

checks.titleEn: ECS instances should not use the default security group
checks.condition: Ensure that Elastic Cloud Server (ECS) instances do not use the default security group, which may have overly permissive rules.
checks.remediation: Create custom security groups with least-privilege rules and replace the default security group on all ECS instances.

checks.titleEn: ECS instances should not have public IP addresses
checks.condition: Ensure that Elastic Cloud Server (ECS) instances do not have public IP addresses assigned, reducing exposure to the internet.
checks.remediation: Remove public IP addresses from ECS instances. Use NAT Gateways or VPN connections for instances that require outbound internet access, and Load Balancers for inbound access.

checks.titleEn: ECS instances should have security groups attached
checks.condition: Ensure that Elastic Cloud Server (ECS) instances have at least one security group attached to control network traffic.
checks.remediation: Attach at least one properly configured security group to every ECS instance.

checks.titleEn: ELB load balancers should not have public IP addresses
checks.condition: Ensure that Elastic Load Balancer (ELB) instances do not have public IP addresses unless explicitly required, to reduce the attack surface.
checks.remediation: Avoid assigning public IP addresses to ELB load balancers unless they are intended to be internet-facing.

checks.titleEn: EVS volumes are encrypted
checks.condition: Ensure that all Huawei Cloud Elastic Volume Service (EVS) disks are encrypted to protect data at rest.
checks.remediation: Enable encryption for all EVS volumes using a KMS key.

checks.titleEn: IAM password policy requires a minimum length of 14 or greater
checks.condition: Huawei Cloud IAM password policies can be used to enforce password complexity requirements. It is recommended that the password policy require a minimum of 14 or greater characters for any password. Longer passwords provide exponentially more security against automated password cracking, as the keyspace increases dramatically with each additional character.
checks.remediation: Configure the IAM password policy to require a minimum password length of 14 characters or greater.

checks.titleEn: IAM password policy requires at least 3 character types
checks.condition: Huawei Cloud IAM password policies can enforce character complexity by requiring multiple character types (uppercase, lowercase, digits, special characters). It is recommended that at least 3 character types be required to increase password strength.
checks.remediation: Configure the IAM password policy to require at least 3 character types in passwords.

checks.titleEn: IAM password policy requires passwords to expire
checks.condition: Huawei Cloud IAM password policies can enforce password expiration. It is recommended that the password validity period be set to a non-zero value so that passwords must be rotated periodically, reducing the window of opportunity for compromised credentials.
checks.remediation: Configure the IAM password policy to require password expiration by setting a non-zero password validity period.

checks.titleEn: IAM password policy enforces a minimum password age
checks.condition: Huawei Cloud IAM password policies can enforce a minimum password age, preventing users from changing passwords too frequently. This works in conjunction with password reuse prevention to ensure users cannot cycle through disallowed passwords to reuse an old one.
checks.remediation: Configure the IAM password policy to enforce a minimum password age of at least 1 day.

checks.titleEn: IAM password policy prevents reuse of at least 3 previous passwords
checks.condition: Huawei Cloud IAM password policies can prevent users from reusing recent passwords. It is recommended that the policy disallow reuse of at least the last 3 passwords to ensure users choose new passwords upon rotation.
checks.remediation: Configure the IAM password policy to disallow reuse of at least the last 3 passwords.

checks.titleEn: Root account enforces MFA through operation protection
checks.condition: The Huawei Cloud account (root/domain owner) should enforce MFA. Because the domain owner is not a listable IAM user, root MFA is assessed through the account's operation protection policy, which requires MFA verification (virtual MFA, SMS, or email) before critical operations such as deleting resources or managing credentials can be performed.
checks.remediation: Enable operation protection for the account and avoid using root credentials for daily operations.

checks.titleEn: IAM disabled users are reviewed and removed if stale
checks.condition: Disabled IAM user accounts that are no longer needed should be removed to reduce the attack surface. Stale disabled accounts may still have associated resources, permissions, or access keys that could be exploited if re-enabled.
checks.remediation: Review disabled IAM users and remove accounts that are no longer needed.

checks.titleEn: IAM users have MFA enabled
checks.condition: Huawei Cloud IAM users should have MFA enabled. MFA adds an extra layer of protection on top of a username and password. With MFA enabled, when a user signs in to the Huawei Cloud console, they are prompted for their username and password as well as for an authentication code from their MFA device.
checks.remediation: Enable MFA for all IAM users and enforce MFA at the account level.

checks.titleEn: KMS keys are not in pending deletion state
checks.condition: Huawei Cloud Key Management Service (KMS) keys that are in PendingDeletion state should be reviewed. Keys scheduled for deletion may cause decryption failures for dependent resources, leading to data unavailability. Ensure deletion is intentional and all dependent resources have been migrated.
checks.remediation: Review KMS keys in pending deletion state and cancel deletion if the key is still needed.

checks.titleEn: KMS keys have rotation enabled
checks.condition: Ensure that Huawei Cloud Key Management Service (KMS) keys have automatic key rotation enabled to regularly rotate the cryptographic material.
checks.remediation: Enable automatic key rotation for all KMS keys.

checks.titleEn: OBS buckets are not publicly accessible
checks.condition: Ensure that Object Storage Service (OBS) buckets are not publicly accessible to prevent unauthorized access to stored objects.
checks.remediation: Remove public access permissions from OBS buckets and use IAM policies for controlled access.

checks.titleEn: RDS instances have automated backup enabled
checks.condition: Ensure that Huawei Cloud Relational Database Service (RDS) instances have automatic backup enabled to protect against data loss.
checks.remediation: Enable automated backup for all RDS instances with an appropriate retention period.

checks.titleEn: RDS instances should have disk encryption enabled
checks.condition: Ensure that Huawei Cloud Relational Database Service (RDS) instances have storage disk encryption enabled using a Key Management Service (KMS) key.
checks.remediation: Enable disk encryption on all RDS instances using a customer-managed KMS key.

checks.titleEn: RDS instances are not publicly accessible
checks.condition: Ensure that Huawei Cloud Relational Database Service (RDS) instances do not have public IP addresses to prevent direct internet access to databases.
checks.remediation: Remove public IP addresses from RDS instances and use VPC peering or VPN for access.

checks.titleEn: SMN topics have at least one confirmed subscription
checks.condition: Ensure that SMN notification topics have at least one confirmed subscription so alerts can be delivered to recipients.
checks.remediation: Add and confirm at least one subscription for each SMN topic so notifications can be delivered.

checks.titleEn: Default security groups restrict all traffic
checks.condition: Ensure that default security groups restrict all traffic to prevent unauthorized access to cloud resources.
checks.remediation: Remove or restrict security group rules that allow traffic from open CIDR ranges (0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0). Default security groups should not allow unrestricted inbound or outbound traffic.

checks.titleEn: VPC security groups should not allow ingress from 0.0.0.0/0 on all ports/protocols
checks.condition: Ensure that Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) security groups do not have ingress rules that allow all protocols from 0.0.0.0/0 (i.e., rules with no port range specified).
checks.remediation: Replace any ingress rule allowing all protocols from 0.0.0.0/0 with specific port and IP range restrictions following least-privilege principles.

checks.titleEn: VPC security groups do not allow open egress to the internet
checks.condition: Security groups should not allow unrestricted egress to all destinations. Huawei Cloud represents unrestricted destinations as 0.0.0.0/0, ::/0, or an empty remote IP prefix without a remote security group or address group. Open egress allows instances to reach any destination on the internet, increasing the risk of data exfiltration and command-and-control communication.
checks.remediation: Restrict allow egress rules to required destination IP ranges, security groups, or address groups instead of allowing all IPv4 or IPv6 destinations.

checks.titleEn: VPC security groups do not allow open ingress on sensitive ports
checks.condition: Security groups should not allow ingress from 0.0.0.0/0 on sensitive ports such as SSH (22), RDP (3389), MySQL (3306), Redis (6379), and MongoDB (27017). Open ingress on these ports exposes critical services to the internet and significantly increases the attack surface.
checks.remediation: Restrict ingress rules on sensitive ports to trusted IP ranges instead of 0.0.0.0/0.

checks.titleEn: WAF (Web Application Firewall) is enabled
checks.condition: Ensure that Web Application Firewall (WAF) is enabled to protect web applications from common exploits.
checks.remediation: Enable WAF and configure it to protect all web applications and APIs.
